title: applicationPlugins
summary: Install the optional Preact application Vite integration.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: directory defaults to src/routes; ssr defaults to true; splitRoutes defaults to true. resourceRequest identifies resource URLs that need server handling without an HTML Accept header.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: Returns a Plugin array including flat route discovery, server export filtering, Preact aliases, lazy routes and development HTTP handling.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Install the optional Preact application Vite integration.

sections.title: Behavior and limits
sections.body: The default SSR integration loads src/entry.server.tsx and starts src/entry.client.tsx. ssr: false supports browser-only apps. Production browser builds reject imported *.server.ts/js modules anywhere in the project, including raw imports; SSR builds can use them. This guard does not replace keeping secrets out of ordinary browser modules or restricting development-server access. See the virtual routes guide; these plugins do not create a production Express server.

sections.title: Renderer selection
sections.body: Import applicationPlugins from react/vite or preact/vite. The React entry selects React without compatibility aliases; the Preact entry retains its Preact configuration. Both support SSR middleware, app-scoped transport, lazy file routes and route changes during development.
sections.code:
import { applicationPlugins } from "@kasperrt/smolter/react/vite";

export default { plugins: applicationPlugins() };

sections.title: Request body limit (0.5.2)
sections.body: Node createRequestHandler and Vite applicationPlugins/routerPlugin default to maxBodySize: 1048576 (1 MiB). Oversized declared lengths are rejected before reading; chunked bodies are counted as received and return 413 before application handlers run. The limit includes multipart overhead and counts received bytes, not decompressed content. Configure the same finite, nonnegative integer in production and development for intentionally larger uploads; zero permits only empty bodies. Keep hosting timeouts, rate/concurrency limits and any decompression limits. Low-level webRequest accepts this limit as its fourth argument and throws a Response for policy or size rejection; the provided middleware sends it automatically.
